candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: controlled substances, safe medication handling, administration and security-related medication practices.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — controlled-substance storage and security
candidate.educational_objective: Apply federal DEA physical-security requirements by storing Schedule II–V controlled substances in securely locked, substantially constructed storage that meets applicable DEA requirements.

options.A: Store Schedule II–V substances on open shelving inside a locked clinic room because the locked room alone satisfies the cabinet requirement.
options.B: Keep Schedule II–V substances in an unlocked medication cart during operating hours when licensed clinicians are working on the unit.
options.C: Use one shared access key for all employees so medications remain available while access restrictions are handled through end-of-day inventory.
options.D: Store Schedule II–V controlled substances in a securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet or other storage meeting applicable DEA security requirements.

candidate.rationale: DEA guidance applying 21 CFR 1301.75(b) states that controlled substances stored at a practitioner's registered location must be kept in a securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet, subject to applicable DEA security requirements. DEA also states that Schedule II–V controlled substances may be stored in a safe or securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: At a DEA-registered practice location, controlled substances must be secured in storage meeting DEA physical-security requirements, including a securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet under 21 CFR 1301.75(b).
candidate.source_document_title: Controlled Substance Security Q&A — Civil Unrest/Looting Registration Guidance Documents Q&A
candidate.source_locator: Practitioners Q&A: continue to comply with 21 CFR 1301.75(b), which requires all controlled substances to be stored in a securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet. Pharmacy Q&A: Schedule II, III, IV and V may be stored in a safe or securely locked, substantially constructed cabinet.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Diversion Control Division
candidate.source_version_date: DEA guidance EO-DEA155/EO-DEA165, June 2020; 21 CFR 1301.75(b) applicability live-rechecked August 16, 2026
